item.title: Scotland men slip up at European curling before semi-finals live on BBC
item.description: Scotland's women are next up against Lithuania on Friday afternoon [Getty Images] Scotland's men will face unbeaten Sweden in the European Curling Championships semi-finals after losing their 100% record in the round-robin following a disappointing 6-5 defeat by Italy. It means that Grant Hardie's rink finish second in Group A behind Stefano Spiller's side, who face the Czech Republic in the other semi-final. World and Olympic champion Oskar Eriksson's Swedes beat Poland 7-2 to secure top place in Group B with a 100% record, while Lukas Klima's Czechs qualified as runners-up despite losing their second match of the round robin - 8-4 to Sergio Vez's Spain. Against Italy, the Scots were always playing catch-up after losing two at the opening end. Hardie's rink did manage to edge ahead at 4-3 after the sixth end, but Italy took two at the seventh and, although the Scots then levelled to take the match into an extra-end, lead Ross Whyte was short with his final stone to concede defeat. Before the men's semi-finals, Scotland's women are also in last-four action against Switzerland (12:30 GMT), with both matches live on the BBC iPlayer and online. Fay Henderson's rink clinched a place in the last four with a game to spare after a tense extra-end triumph over Estonia on Thursday. Having suffered their first defeat of the group stage earlier, losing 10-2 to Sweden, they hit back from 8-3 down to score three and then steal two to force an extra end. Then Scotland managed a crucial steal to win it 9-8 when Estonia skip Marie Kaldvee was unable to clear a Scottish stone with a raise-takeout. Fay Henderson's rink ended off their Group B campaign with a 7-5 victory over Lithuania as they qualified as runners-up behind Isabella Wranaa's Swede's. Alina Paetz, who won world and European gold in 2023, led her Swiss to five straight wins to top of Group A ahead of Evelina Barone's Latvians. item.title: ‘That’s not right’ – Jerry Jones called out by Super Bowl winner over Troy Aikman suggestion
item.description: Photo by Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images Troy Aikman’s future with ESPN is looking less and less certain by the day with some suggesting the Dallas Cowboys should look to bring him back into the building. The extent of Aikman’s debacle with ESPN continues to come to light with new revelations being shared by the media almost daily. Given his contract expires at the end of the season, it now feels unlikely that a deal will be agreed to keep him on Monday Night Football. Jerry Jones was spotted speaking to Aikman ahead of the Cowboys’ Monday Night Football victory over the Philadelphia Eagles recently. This has sparked suggestions that something could be in the works between the pair to bring Aikman back to Dallas in the future. Jerry Jones questioned over possible Troy Aikman hire with Dallas Cowboys Former New England Patriots and Eagles cornerback Asante Samuel has hit out at Jones over potentially bringing back Aikman, but not Michael Irvin. The 60-year-old, Irvin, has also become a regular on ESPN but there has been no suggestion Jones wants him back at the Cowboys. “How can Jerry Jones hire Troy Aikman and not bring Michael Irvin along? That’s not right,” said Samuel on X. The issue Jones may have – if he wants Aikman with the Cowboys – is that there could be a number of different networks already looking to pounce on the former quarterback’s ESPN debacle. It has become very messy for Aikman, with his relationships at ESPN taking a real blow. There is also the possibility that the contract saga may also have pushed Aikman away from broadcasting. However, he is unlikely to find a role in the NFL that pays as highly as his ESPN gig did. Jones is notorious for not investing heavily in his staff. The billionaire has no issues paying his players, but he often draws the line at spending considerable money on his staff. This could certainly be an issue if he does want Aikman back in the building. item.title: What's the youth path to the USMNT? How U.S. Soccer wants to widen it
item.description: USA TODAY Sports spoke with the U.S. Soccer Federation and Major League Soccer about the state of the American youth game and the pipeline to the top following last summer’s World Cup. Since its Round of 16 finish, the USMNT has gone 4-0 in fall friendlies and plays next in the Concacaf Nations League two-legged November quarterfinal series against Haiti . The USA has been boosted by an influx of youth . We explore how to create opportunities for every young soccer player so they can find their personal path. Read Part 1: Three ways to improve a kid’s youth soccer experience from the beginning Part II: How does the path to the USMNT work, and how can we widen it? There are childhood moments to which we can point that define our sports careers. For Ali Curtis, now president of MLS NEXT Pro , one of them came when he was about 9. He was a top player at his age, and he tried out for a local team full of kids two years older than him. He remembers being told he wasn’t going to make the team, as he was too small or too young. “In your own mind, you're always probably a better player than you think you are,” he says, “but I thought I was one of the top players at the tryouts." Before Curtis left the soccer complex, someone directed him toward another team in Livonia, Michigan, which was about 40 minutes away from where he lived. He joined the team, which connected him back to his age group but had a competitive environment. “That was probably the most difficult moment that I had in my career or my soccer journey at the time,” he says. “But it happened to be the best thing that ever happened to me. I went and played for that team and was off to the races after that in terms of everything that happened in my youth soccer career and journey.” When he made a regional team at around 14, Curtis was required to go on an international trip. But his mother said they couldn’t afford it. Curtis, now 47, remembers his coaches finding a way to fund the trip, which cleared his pathway to a national team, and eventually, Major League Soccer , which began in 1996. As U.S. Soccer seeks to widen its pool of potential players, would Curtis emerge on the national radar today? His story covers at least two issues that are still rampant in youth soccer: high costs that limit access, and coaches' distorted eye toward players who may not be considered top-level on their teams but blossom later. U.S. Soccer is working with its state associations to create a more unified system that will lower costs, provide more meaningful experiences and grow participation. item.title: Colts now open to trading Jonathan Taylor, Giants & Vikings among 5 teams to express interest
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts have reportedly changed their stance on trading star running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the trade deadline. The Colts were reportedly reluctant about trading their best player, but ESPN’s Adam Schefter and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport report that the team is now willing to move him. “The Indianapolis Colts now are open to trading star running back Jonathan Taylor, sources told ESPN and NFL Network,” Schefter and Rapoport wrote on Saturday morning. The NFL insiders added that “multiple teams have reached out to Indianapolis, and those talks are said to be active and ongoing, according to sources.” MORE: Wrestling legends loved Christian Watson’s WWE-style return That second part of the report suggests it might not be long before Taylor is moved. Perhaps we’ll see a trade go down after this weekend, but that obviously hasn’t been confirmed. It just makes sense for the Colts to move Taylor at this point. With the rebuild incoming, the Colts are at least a few years away from competing again and Taylor could start to decline in that span. His value may never be higher than it is now, so trading him is the logical move. 5 teams expressing interest in Taylor Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) rushes the ball against the Minnesota Vikings in the second half at U.S. Bank Stadium. Credit: Brad Rempel-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Included in the report is the five teams that have “expressed at least some level of interest” in Taylor. The list includes the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants and Seattle Seahawks. “The list of teams that have expressed at least some level of interest in trading for Taylor so far is thought to include the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants and Seattle Seahawks, sources said,” the NFL insiders said. The Broncos already have a pretty crowded running backs room with RJ Harvey, J.K. Dobbins and Jonah Coleman, but none of those guys are as talented as Taylor, of course. MORE: ESPN reportedly picks sides in Aikman-Bucks fallout The Giants might have the most dire need of that group, as they have Cam Skattebo and not much else in their running backs room. Minnesota is right there with them with their uninspiring group led by Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason. The Packers recently got back Josh Jacobs, but the veteran running back is now facing more allegations of abuse, according to ESPN , which leaves his outlook murky. Seattle has already swung a big trade with the Colts for Quenton Nelson and could certainly use an upgrade at running back, even with Jadarian Price set to return from injury. No matter where he lands, the former rushing champion is going to amount to a big upgrade. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Inside how Max Eberl knew Vincent Kompany was perfect for Bayern Munich
item.description: (Photo by Sebastian El-Saqqa - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Vincent Kompany was not the obvious choice to succeed Thomas Tuchel at Bayern Munich. He had just suffered relegation with Burnley, and appointing him to lead one of the biggest clubs in world football was a gamble that raised p lenty of eyebrows. Yet, Max Eberl saw something in the Belgian coach that went far beyond the results on his CV. The initial conversation that changed everything Asked whether Kompany was his masterstroke signing, rather than a player, Eberl explained why the appointment would not necessarily have been an easy sell at the time. “I joined the club at a time when it was already cle ar that the coach would not continue beyond the end of the season. Bayern explored several options, including Julian Nagelsmann and Ralf Rangnick, before Eberl decided to contact the former Manchester City captain. “Of cour se, we worked our way through a list of candidates. Julian Nagelsmann was one of them; that’ s no secret. I had a very good relationship with him, but he decided to take the Germany job. item.title: Cannavaro: ‘Spalletti and Allegri are similar, Kolo Muani and Hojlund less killer than strikers of my era’
item.description: Cannavaro: ‘Spalletti and Allegri are similar, Kolo Muani and Hojlund less killer than strikers of my era’ Fabio Cannavaro believes Luciano Spalletti and Massimiliano Allegri have plenty in common, and that Rasmus Højlund and Randal Kolo Muani are not the ruthless strikers of his generation. With quotes via Calciomercato.com , the former defender, who played for both clubs, previewed Sunday’s clash between Juventus and Napoli in an interview with Betsson.Sport. It kicks off at 20:45 CET [19:45 GMT] at the Allianz Stadium. “Spalletti and Allegri are two great coaches who have achieved great results in recent years,” Cannavaro said. “They know Italian football very well and everything that surrounds it: how to manage players, journalists and fans. Tactically, they’re not tied to one system and they know how to adapt to their players.” Allegri will not be on the touchline. He is serving the second game of a two-match ban, so assistant Marco Landucci takes charge again. The sides go into the game level on 14 points, but in very different moods. item.title: Wyndham Clark’s comments about his brother suggest why he missed the cut at the Mexico Open
item.description: Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images Wyndham Clark’s family affair at the Mexico Open did not go to plan. The two-time US Open winner had his brother on the bag in Mexico and hoped to help pay for his wedding with the prize money. Instead, Clark missed the cut by two strokes in one of his worst performances of the season. Clark has been in fine form of late and is in the midst of a bounce back season, so this week was an anomaly. But what he said about his brother in the week’s build-up is a clue as to what happened to his golf game. Wyndham Clark criticized his brother’s caddying ability Clark lost 3.31 strokes to the field on approach, and 1.43 strokes to the field with his putting. These are the two areas of the game where caddying matters most, and they cost Clark in Mexico. That is hardly surprising, considering Clark admitted his brother gave him the wrong yardages the last time he caddied for him at Colonial. Speaking to SiriusXM PGA Tour Radio in the build-up to the Mexico Open, he said, “He ChatGPT’d the stats of the golf course and looked it up relative to my stats, but what was funny is they changed the routing of the golf course, added new holes, so all that went out the window. “He was trying to do all this hard work, and none of it was going to help.” It’s hard to know whether Clark’s performance was down to poor caddying or whether he just missed putts and his swing was off, but judging by his comments about his brother, he really could have done with a professional caddie on the bag. item.description: Liverpool v Arsenal - Premier League - Getty Images Sport Relive the breathless drama of April 2009, when Andrey Arshavin struck four times at Anfield to dent Liverpool's Premier League title ambitions in a remarkable 4-4 draw. Braces from Fernando Torres and Yossi Benayoun rescued a late point for Rafael Benitez's side, yet the night belonged to Arsenal's clinical Russian forward. There are rare nights under the Anfield floodlights when tactical orthodoxy dissolves into pure, unscripted theatre. In April 2009, with the Premier League title race reaching breaking point, 44,424 spectators witnessed an eight-goal duel that defied all defensive logic. Watched from the stands by Liverpool's joint owners Tom Hicks and George Gillett, two of England's great heavyweights traded blows until neither side could stand. The siege of Anfield and the Russian twist The siege of Anfield and the Russian twist Without their talismanic captain Steven Gerrard, Benitez's side still began with ferocious intent, pinning Arsene Wenger's visitors deep inside their own half. Spearheaded by a relentless Torres, the hosts laid siege to goal, only to find an unlikely barrier in Lukasz Fabianski. Heavily criticised after an FA Cup semi-final defeat just days earlier, the Polish keeper produced an inspired first-half display, twice denying Torres before palming away Benayoun's drive. Football, however, rarely rewards dominance without ruthlessness. Nine minutes before the interval, Javier Mascherano was caught in possession, allowing Samir Nasri and Cesc Fabregas to carve open the home defence for Arshavin to crash a finish off the underside of the bar. item.description: Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images Steph Curry dropping Luka Doncic to the floor was the highlight of the Golden State Warriors’ NBA Cup win against the Los Angeles Lakers. Everybody is talking about Curry’s ankle-breaker on Doncic, including the Slovenian’s new rival, Yaxel Lendeborg. At times, the Wildcats looked like the better team but struggled to pull away from the Knights. UCF eventually took the lead in the final minutes of regulation before Kentucky guard Alex Wilkins hit a game-tying shot to send the contest into overtime. Kentucky then dominated the extra period, outscoring UCF 14-5. The performance showed that if the Wildcats can put everything together, they have the potential to be one of the better teams in the country. item.description: Max Verstappen finished FP2 in Mexico with damage to his car and the fifth-fastest time. His longer run gives Red Bull Racing something to build on, as he was close to George Russell . For now, it remains unclear how much faster Verstappen could be with a repaired car. His run also did not include the later phase, when several rivals began to lose pace. Verstappen made contact with Liam Lawson in FP1, and the incident affected the rest of his session. Technical director Pierre Waché confirmed that the damage had hurt performance and would be repaired in time for FP3. He felt the long run was reasonably solid, but also saw room to work on the balance. Neither driver was satisfied with it yet. Verstappen finds his pace again after a slower lap Despite that, Verstappen’s average of 1:21.490 on the soft tyre is reasonably encouraging. Russell recorded 1:21.442 on the same compound, a difference of just 0.048 seconds. Lando Norris was a little bit quicker with 1:21.319. One notable feature of Verstappen’s run is that after an opening lap of 1:21.963, he completed three laps between 1:21.170 and 1:21.260. Those laps were closely grouped. Even after a break and a slower 1:22.020, he returned to his earlier pace with a 1:21.276. His final recorded lap was a 1:21.523. There it is also important to point out that Verstappen only did seven laps. Russell and Norris did nine and eleven, respectively. The New England Patriots have a defensive problem that cannot be explained simply by looking at points allowed or the standings. Through seven games, New England has performed like one of the NFL's best defenses when playing man coverage. When the Patriots switch to zone, however, the results have been dramatically different. That split could become one of the most important storylines when Mike Vrabel's team visits the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. According to statistics published in the Patriots' official Week 8 gameplan analysis, New England ranks third in the NFL in expected points added per pass play when playing man coverage. In zone, the Patriots rank 30th. For a team hoping to build momentum in the AFC East, that is a difficult discrepancy to ignore. Two Defenses Wearing The Same Uniform The numbers become even more revealing when pressure is included. New England generates pressure on 50% of opposing dropbacks when playing man coverage, the second-best rate in the league. In zone coverage, that number falls to 29.1%, ranking 31st. The Patriots have relied on aggressive pressure packages to disrupt opposing quarterbacks, but that approach becomes more complicated when defenders must protect space rather than follow individual receivers. Zone coverage often requires a dependable four-man pass rush. Without it, quarterbacks have time to identify openings between defenders. That creates a difficult decision for Vrabel's staff. The Patriots can lean into what they do best, but the quarterback waiting in Miami presents an unusual challenge. The Patriots' official scouting analysis notes that Willis has been more efficient against man coverage and blitzes than against zone defenses this season. That is precisely the opposite of what New England's overall defensive statistics might encourage the coaching staff to do. Willis can escape pressure, extend plays and punish defenders who turn their backs while following receivers. Miami also uses extensive pre-snap motion and a creative running game to stress defensive assignments.
